summary: Add an opt-in RADIUS accounting listener MVP that can be developed and tested without root, decode common accounting packets, and prepare dynamic-circuit command plumbing for lqosd integration.

stories.title: Create the lqos_radius crate
stories.description: As a LibreQoS developer, I want a separate lqos_radius crate with a rootless test executable, so that RADIUS accounting protocol work can be built and exercised without running lqosd as root.
acceptanceCriteria: The Rust workspace includes lqos_radius as a buildable member.
lqos_radius exposes a library API for packet handling and listener startup.
lqos_radius includes an executable entrypoint that can run on a configurable non-privileged listen address.
cargo test for lqos_radius runs without requiring root privileges or live shaping state.

stories.title: Configure RADIUS accounting
stories.description: As a LibreQoS operator, I want RADIUS accounting settings in LibreQoS configuration, so that I can explicitly enable the listener and control which NAS clients are trusted.
acceptanceCriteria: radius_accounting can be disabled without requiring any RADIUS clients.
When radius_accounting is enabled, configuration requires a valid listen address and at least one client source.
Each configured client has a source allow-list and a shared secret source that is not emitted in logs or serialized debug output.
Configuration validation rejects invalid listen addresses, invalid client sources, missing secrets, and non-positive timing values.
Configuration round-trip tests cover enabled and disabled RADIUS accounting settings.

stories.title: Decode and verify accounting packets
stories.description: As a LibreQoS operator, I want incoming RADIUS accounting packets to be decoded and verified, so that only authentic Accounting-Request packets from trusted clients are accepted.
acceptanceCriteria: The decoder accepts Accounting-Request packets and rejects unsupported RADIUS packet codes for this MVP.
Packet length, attribute bounds, and malformed attribute cases are validated before packet acceptance.
Accounting-Request authenticators are verified against the matched client shared secret.
Message-Authenticator is verified when present and is required when configuration enables that policy.
Valid accepted requests can produce an Accounting-Response packet with response code 5.

stories.title: Extract common accounting attributes
stories.description: As a LibreQoS operator, I want common RADIUS accounting attributes translated into typed session events, so that subscriber session lifecycle, identity, and address data can be inspected and used later.
acceptanceCriteria: Typed events include Acct-Status-Type values for Start, Stop, Interim-Update, Accounting-On, and Accounting-Off.

Typed events include session and NAS identity fields such as Acct-Session-Id, NAS-IP-Address, NAS-IPv6-Address, NAS-Identifier, NAS-Port, NAS-Port-Id, User-Name, Calling-Station-Id, Called-Station-Id, Class, and Event-Timestamp when present.
Typed events include subscriber address fields such as Framed-IP-Address, Framed-IP-Netmask, Framed-Route, Framed-IPv6-Prefix, Delegated-IPv6-Prefix, and Framed-IPv6-Address when present.
Unknown standard attributes and unknown vendor-specific attributes are preserved for diagnostics without rejecting otherwise valid packets.
MikroTik-Rate-Limit vendor attributes are decoded into rate values and tests verify configurable NAS-to-LibreQoS direction mapping.

stories.title: Run a rootless UDP accounting listener
stories.description: As a LibreQoS developer, I want the lqos_radius listener to run against loopback test traffic, so that protocol and server behavior can be proven before wiring live lqosd behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: The listener can bind to 127.0.0.1:0 or another configured non-privileged address for tests.
Accepted Accounting-Request packets receive an Accounting-Response without waiting for dynamic-circuit application.
Packets from unconfigured sources do not create session events or command placeholders.
Packets with invalid authenticators are rejected and do not create session events or command placeholders.
Loopback UDP tests verify accepted requests, rejected sources, invalid authenticators, and response behavior.

stories.title: Track accounting sessions in memory
stories.description: As a LibreQoS operator, I want accepted accounting events to update runtime session state, so that Starts, Interims, Stops, and NAS resets have predictable results during the MVP.
acceptanceCriteria: Sessions are keyed primarily by NAS identity plus Acct-Session-Id when both values are available.
Start and Interim-Update events create or refresh a session and preserve the latest decoded identity and address data.
Stop events mark the session stopped and are harmless when duplicated.
Accounting-On and Accounting-Off mark sessions for the affected NAS stale without affecting other NAS clients.
Sessions that cannot become dynamic circuits retain a specific pending reason such as missing IP, missing rate, missing parent, missing session ID, or ambiguous mapping.

stories.title: Prepare dynamic-circuit command plumbing
stories.description: As a LibreQoS developer, I want RADIUS session handling to emit create, update, and remove command placeholders, so that lqosd can later connect those commands to the existing dynamic-circuit path without changing the protocol server.
acceptanceCriteria: lqos_radius exposes a command sink boundary for dynamic-circuit intents that the lqosd-facing adapter can map to CreateDynamicCircuit and RemoveDynamicCircuit placeholders.
Shapeable Start and Interim-Update events emit create or update command intents through the sink boundary.
Stop events emit remove command intents when a deterministic circuit identity is available.
Fake sink tests assert the emitted command type and circuit identity for Start, Interim-Update, Stop, and expiry scenarios.
The listener never writes dynamic_circuits.json directly.

stories.title: Start the listener from lqosd when configured
stories.description: As a LibreQoS operator, I want lqosd to start the RADIUS accounting listener only when configured, so that existing installations are unchanged unless RADIUS accounting is enabled.
acceptanceCriteria: lqosd does not bind a RADIUS accounting socket when radius_accounting is absent or disabled.
When radius_accounting is enabled, lqosd starts the listener inside the existing tokio runtime after configuration is loaded.
Listener startup failures are reported clearly without logging shared secrets.
lqosd shutdown stops the listener without blocking daemon shutdown.
The lqosd wiring uses the lqos_radius command sink boundary and leaves final dynamic-circuit application behind the existing bus or daemon channel path for this MVP.

stories.title: Provide protocol test fixtures
stories.description: As a LibreQoS developer, I want focused protocol fixtures and scenario tests, so that regressions in packet parsing, authentication, and listener behavior are caught without NAS hardware.
acceptanceCriteria: Raw packet fixtures cover valid Accounting-Start, Accounting-Interim, Accounting-Stop, invalid packet length, invalid authenticator, unknown standard attributes, unknown vendor-specific attributes, and IPv6 address or prefix attributes.
A test packet builder can generate authenticated Accounting-Request packets for readable scenario tests.

Authenticator tests cover correct secrets, wrong secrets, modified attributes, truncated packets, valid Message-Authenticator, invalid Message-Authenticator, and required Message-Authenticator policy.
Session tests use fake time and a fake command sink instead of sockets, root privileges, bakery, TC, XDP, or disk writes.

notes: Full dynamic-circuit application, operator UI or CLI diagnostics, persistent session storage, and CoA or Disconnect support remain outside this MVP unless separately requested.
Binding the default UDP 1813 port may require elevated privileges; the crate executable and automated tests should support non-privileged addresses for development.
